newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho issues first-half profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho issues first-half profits warning.

text.p: Lonrho Plc said on Monday that profits before tax of continuing businesses for the six months to March 31 "could be around one third down on the previous year".

Lonrho said in a statement that the strength of sterling, poor precious metal prices, lower profits at Ashanti and moderate results in its African trading businesses would "adversely affect the results of the companies continuing businesses".

In January Lonrho, which is undergoing a demerger, reported a 12.6 percent rise in full-year pre-tax profits. Last week British newspapers reported that Lonrho looked unlikley to be able to sell its Princess hotel chain in one go.
Analysts said the hotel sale was a necessary step before Lonrho could finally hive of its African trading operations from its mining rump. The group's split was set out over a year ago.
Lonrho recently announced the appointment of John Craven, the former British ambassador to South Africa, as its chairman.
Craven, who is the non-executive chairman of investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, is seen as having the right contacts and skills to complete Lonrho's demerger.

He will succeed Sir John Leahy, and may fill the void left by German businesman Dieter Bock, who initiated Lonrho's demerger process before stepping down as non-executive director to return to the real estate business.

Lonrho initially wanted to demerge its mining operations, then decided to demerge its hotels activities instead only to eventually opt for an outright sale. This divestment would then likely be followed by a demerger of the trading operations, Lonrho said two months ago.
But so far, Lonrho has only realised the 327 million pound sale of its Metropole hotels to Glasgow-based Stakis Plc in September.
Recent newspaper reports suggested Lonrho is now considering to split the Princess hotel chain, while the conglomerate is also said mulling the sale of its African sugar interests.

South African-listed Lonrho Sugar Ltd, in which British Lonrho has a 94 percent stake, said late last month it was holding share-price sensitive talks with third parties, prompting market talk of a takeover.
Lonrho, in which South Africa's Anglo American has a 28 percent stake, was earlier said to be talking to sell the the Princess hotel chain to Saudi Prince al-Waleed bin Talal.
But newspapers now say the Prince is only interested in buying part of the chain, which has hotels in the U.S, Mexico and the Caribbean region.
Lonrho shares were down 11 pence at 146.5 pence at 1342 GMT.
